keywords.nuance: それでも introduces a contrast where one fact does not cancel the next action, or a result still holds despite difficulty.
keywords.example: 高いですが、それでもいいです。
keywords.exampleTranslation: It's expensive, but I'll still buy it anyway.

commonPitfall.title: Common Pitfall
commonPitfall.body: It is similar to でも, but それでも often sets up a stronger contrast between a real obstacle and a final resilient decision.

questions.prompt: 雨が降っている。それでも彼は行く。
questions.answer: It is raining. Even so, he is going.

questions.prompt: 難しいです。それでも続けたい。
questions.answer: It's difficult. I still want to continue.
It was expensive. Still, I bought it.

questions.prompt: 時間がない。それでも、まずは提出する。
questions.answer: There is no time. Even so, submit it first.

productionQuestions.prompt: It's complicated, but let's submit it anyway.
productionQuestions.hint: Useそれでも before taking action despite obstacles.

referenceAnswers.answer: 複雑だけど、それでも提出しよう。
referenceAnswers.note: Very common and natural in study/work contexts.

referenceAnswers.answer: 難しいと思う。それでも一応提出する。
referenceAnswers.note: Adds emotional tone with 一応.

productionQuestions.prompt: The bus is crowded, but we should still get on.
productionQuestions.hint: Use それでも with a practical despite-condition.

referenceAnswers.answer: バスは混んでいるけど、それでも乗る。
混んでいても、それでも行きたい。

productionQuestions.prompt: He said no, but I'll try anyway.
productionQuestions.hint: Express persistence after a discouraging response.

referenceAnswers.answer: 彼に断られた。それでも挑戦してみる。
断られても、それでもやってみる。

productionQuestions.prompt: I was too tired, but I still want to walk.
productionQuestions.hint: Use それでも to preserve intention after fatigue.

referenceAnswers.answer: とても疲れているけど、それでも散歩したい。
疲れている。それでも歩きたい。
referenceAnswers.note: Short, direct, and common in spoken language.
